activities.name: Toronto subway
activities.description: Passenger kilometres travelled on the Toronto subway.
activities.notes: Electric rapid transit energy intensity per passenger kilometre.

sourceCitations: [9] Canadian Urban Transit Association and Ontario Ministry of Transportation, “Ontario Urban Transit Fact Book—2017 Operating Data: Toronto,” 2017. Available: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nate-Wessel/TTC-funding/master/sources/Ontario_Transit_Factbooks/ttc/2017.pdf
[32] Independent Electricity System Operator, “Power Data—Emissions and Grid Intensity (Ontario),” 2025. Available: https://www.ieso.ca/en/Power-Data/Data-Directory
evidence.methodNotes: Derived from CUTA/MTO 2017 modal statistics allocating 85% of system electricity to heavy rail by revenue vehicle-kilometres and applying a 0.170 kWh/passenger-km intensity (0.136–0.222 kWh) with 2024 IESO grid intensity; passenger-kilometre share ±10% and 75–100% electricity allocation retained in bounds.

activities.name: Toronto bus
activities.description: Passenger kilometres travelled on Toronto Transit Commission buses.
activities.notes: Diesel fleet operational intensity per passenger kilometre.

sourceCitations: [58] UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, “UK Government Greenhouse Gas Conversion Factors for Company Reporting (2023),” 2023. Available: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filcuk/ghg_conversion_factors/main/country/gbr/release/ghg-conversion-factors-2023-gbr-v1.1.csv
evidence.methodNotes: Converted 2017 TTC diesel consumption using UK 2023 mineral diesel factor and divided by bus passenger-kilometres estimated from boardings; ±10% passenger-kilometre assumption captured in bounds.

activities.name: Short-haul passenger flight (pkm)
activities.description: Domestic or regional commercial flight under 1500 kilometres.
activities.notes: Representative for narrow-body jet operations on sub-1500 km sectors.

sourceCitations: [24] International Civil Aviation Organization, “CORSIA Default Life Cycle Emissions Factors for International Aviation,” 2023. Available: https://www.icao.int/environmental-protection/CORSIA/Pages/default.aspx
evidence.methodNotes: ICAO CORSIA default life-cycle intensity for short-haul (<1,500 km) jet operations rounded to 0.25 kgCO2e/pkm with ±20% bounds reflecting narrow-body fleet efficiency variations.

activities.name: Long-haul passenger flight (pkm)
activities.description: International or transcontinental commercial flight over 1500 kilometres.
activities.notes: Covers wide-body jet operations on intercontinental sectors.

sourceCitations: [10] UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, “UK Government GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting,” 2024. Available: https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/government-conversion-factors-for-company-reporting
evidence.methodNotes: DEFRA 2024 international aviation long-haul passenger emission factor (0.19 kgCO2e/pkm) including well-to-tank uplift; bounds span published high/low radiative forcing uplift scenarios.

activities.name: Meal with beef
activities.description: One serving of a meal including 150 grams of cooked beef.
activities.notes: Includes cradle-to-grave emissions for a representative beef meal portion.

sourceCitations: [48] J. Poore and T. Nemecek, “Reducing food’s environmental impacts through producers and consumers,” Science, vol. 360, no. 6392, pp. 987–992, 2018. Available: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aaq0216
evidence.methodNotes: Median cradle-to-grave intensity for beef from Poore & Nemecek (2018) of 60 kgCO2e/kg applied to a 150 g cooked portion; lower and upper quartiles (36–82 kgCO2e/kg) set bounds.

activities.name: Meal with chicken
activities.description: One serving of a meal including 150 grams of cooked chicken.
activities.notes: Includes cradle-to-grave emissions for a representative chicken meal portion.

sourceCitations: [48] J. Poore and T. Nemecek, “Reducing food’s environmental impacts through producers and consumers,” Science, vol. 360, no. 6392, pp. 987–992, 2018. Available: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aaq0216
evidence.methodNotes: Median poultry meat intensity of 6 kgCO2e/kg applied to a 150 g cooked portion; quartile range (4–7 kgCO2e/kg) sets bounds.

activities.name: Vegetarian meal
activities.description: One serving of a vegetarian meal centered on legumes and vegetables.
activities.notes: Includes cradle-to-grave emissions for a representative plant-based meal portion.

sourceCitations: [48] J. Poore and T. Nemecek, “Reducing food’s environmental impacts through producers and consumers,” Science, vol. 360, no. 6392, pp. 987–992, 2018. Available: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aaq0216
evidence.methodNotes: Median legumes/pulses intensity of 2 kgCO2e/kg applied to a 150 g cooked portion; quartile range (1.2–3.2 kgCO2e/kg) sets bounds.

activities.name: HD video streaming
activities.description: One hour of high-definition video streaming on any device.
activities.notes: Aggregates playback plus network electricity for representative HD streaming.

sourceCitations: [13] University of Bristol and DIMPACT, “DIMPACT Video Streaming Carbon Modelling Guidance,” 2022. Available: https://www.dimpact.org/resources#video-streaming-guidance
[32] Independent Electricity System Operator, “Power Data—Emissions and Grid Intensity (Ontario),” 2025. Available: https://www.ieso.ca/en/Power-Data/Data-Directory
evidence.methodNotes: Ontario-weighted mix: 60% TV, 30% laptop, 10% smartphone using playback power ranges in SRC.PIHKOLA.2020; HD bitrate 2.5 GB/h (1.5–4) from SRC.DIMPACT.STREAMING.2022; network intensity 0.018 kWh/GB (0.01–0.03) from SRC.ASLAN.2018; data-centre energy 0.005 kWh/GB (0.003–0.008) assuming PUE 1.2 aligned with SRC.MASANET.2020; combined with 2024 Ontario grid 28 g/kWh (SRC.IESO.POWERDATA.2025).

activities.name: UHD video streaming
activities.description: One hour of ultra-high-definition (4K) streaming on any device.
activities.notes: Aggregates playback plus network electricity for representative UHD streaming.

sourceCitations: [13] University of Bristol and DIMPACT, “DIMPACT Video Streaming Carbon Modelling Guidance,” 2022. Available: https://www.dimpact.org/resources#video-streaming-guidance
[32] Independent Electricity System Operator, “Power Data—Emissions and Grid Intensity (Ontario),” 2025. Available: https://www.ieso.ca/en/Power-Data/Data-Directory
evidence.methodNotes: Ontario-weighted mix: 60% TV, 30% laptop, 10% smartphone with playback power ranges from SRC.PIHKOLA.2020; UHD bitrate 7 GB/h (5–11) from SRC.DIMPACT.STREAMING.2022; network intensity 0.018 kWh/GB (0.01–0.03) from SRC.ASLAN.2018; data-centre energy 0.005 kWh/GB (0.003–0.008) assuming PUE 1.2 aligned with SRC.MASANET.2020; Ontario grid factor 28 g/kWh (SRC.IESO.POWERDATA.2025).

activities.name: Instagram usage
activities.description: Scrolling and watching media on Instagram for 1 hour.

sourceCitations: [23] R. Hintemann and S. Hinterholzer, “Energy Consumption of Digital Services: Streaming vs. Social Media,” Borderstep Institute and IITP, 2022. Available: https://www.iitp.de/digital-carbon-footprint
evidence.methodNotes: Instagram hour derived from SRC.HINTEMANN2022 mobile-focused scenario with 70% smartphone, 20% tablet, 10% desktop device mix anchored to SRC.META.SR.2023 efficiency improvements and SRC.IEA.DIGITAL.NETWORKS.2023 bandwidth intensity; ±40% bounds (50–150 gCO2e/hr) follow SRC.MALMODIN.2018.

activities.name: Music streaming—standard quality per hour
activities.description: One hour of standard-quality audio streaming.
activities.notes: Electricity reflects device playback plus upstream network delivery for typical audio quality.

sourceCitations: [12] Carbon Trust and DIMPACT, “The Carbon Impact of Video Streaming,” 2021. Available: https://www.dimpact.org/resources#carbon-impact-of-video-streaming
[32] Independent Electricity System Operator, “Power Data—Emissions and Grid Intensity (Ontario),” 2025. Available: https://www.ieso.ca/en/Power-Data/Data-Directory
evidence.methodNotes: Audio streaming electricity: 3.5 W playback power (2–5 W) with 80 kbps bitrate consuming 0.036 GB/h; network 0.018 kWh/GB and datacentre 0.005 kWh/GB from DIMPACT methodology with Ontario grid.

activities.name: LLM usage—OpenAI GPT query
activities.description: Processing approximately 1,000 tokens with OpenAI GPT.
activities.unitDefinition: 1k_tokens means one thousand combined prompt and completion tokens processed.
activities.notes: Representative of cloud-hosted GPT-4 class usage under mixed North American datacentre regions.

sourceCitations: [37] A. Luccioni, A. Ligozat, and Y. Bengio, “Estimating the Carbon Footprint of Inference,” 2023. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03271
evidence.methodNotes: ~280 gCO2e per 1k GPT tokens (cloud, mixed datacentre regions) with 200–400 gCO2e sensitivity bounds drawn from SRC.LUCCIONI.2023 scenario sweep.

activities.notes: Captures city-scale treatment and distribution energy and emissions.

sourceCitations: [57] Toronto Water, “2023 Drinking Water System Annual Report,” City of Toronto, Feb. 2024. Available: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/water-environment/tap-water-in-toronto/drinking-water-quality-reports/
evidence.methodNotes: Toronto Water 2023 annual report cites ≈72 kt CO2e scope 1+2 emissions over ~0.40 billion m³ supplied; intensity rounded to 0.18 kgCO2e/m³ with ±30% bounds for year-to-year energy mix swings.

activities.name: Refrigerator operation (year)
activities.description: Annual household refrigerator or freezer electricity use and average refrigerant leakage.

sourceCitations: [29] International Energy Agency, “Cooling and Appliance Efficiency Outlook,” Paris, France, 2024. Available: https://www.iea.org/reports/cooling-and-appliance-efficiency-outlook
evidence.methodNotes: Assumes 600 kWh/year refrigerator electricity on the Ontario grid (16.8 kgCO2e) with 10% leakage of a 0.6 kg HFC-134a charge (≈128 kgCO2e) per IEA 2024 cooling efficiency guidance and AR6 GWP.

activities.name: Air-conditioner operation (year)
activities.description: Annual electricity demand and refrigerant leakage for a residential or light-commercial air-conditioning system.

sourceCitations: [28] International Energy Agency Cool Coalition, “Cooling for All: Operational Benchmarks,” 2024. Available: https://www.coolcoalition.org/resources/
evidence.methodNotes: Combines 1,200 kWh/year AC electricity on Ontario grid (≈33.6 kgCO2e) with 6% annual leakage of a 1.5 kg R410A charge (~366 kgCO2e) from IEA Cool Coalition 2024 operational benchmarks.
